content: The combination of emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir alafenamide is approved as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults who are treatment-naïve and have an HIV-1 RNA level of ≤100,000 copies/mL. It is also indicated for certain virologically suppressed patients (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) who are on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen at the start of therapy, to replace their current ART regimen. The recommended dose is one tablet (containing emtricitabine 200 mg, rilpivirine 25 mg, and tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg) taken orally once daily with food. This regimen is also approved for adolescents aged 12 years or older who weigh at least 35 kg and meet the same criteria. However, its safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 12 years of age or those weighing less than 35 kg. Drug Interactions: 1. Carbamazepine: Decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 2. Dexamethasone: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated for the same reasons as carbamazepine. 3. Dexlansoprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 4. Efavirenz: Decreases rilpivirine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: This combination is a complete HIV regimen and should not be used with other antiretrovirals, including rilpivirine. 6. Eslicarbazepine acetate: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Esomeprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Etravirine: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Fosphenytoin: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Lansoprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Nevirapine: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Omeprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Oxcarbazepine: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Pantoprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Phenobarbital: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Phenytoin: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Rabeprazole: Increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Rifampin: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Rifapentine: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. St. John’s Wort: Decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Vonoprazan: Reduces rilpivirine absorption. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. QTc-Prolonging Drugs: Rilpivirine increases the QTc interval, and co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs (e.g., amiodarone, azithromycin, citalopram, and others) should be approached with caution. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration cannot be avoided. 23. Antacids: Decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 24. H2 Antagonists: Decrease rilpivirine levels. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 25. Didanosine: Co-administration requires careful timing due to food and gastric pH effects. Didanosine should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 26. CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Drugs like clarithromycin and erythromycin increase rilpivirine levels. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 27. CYP3A4 Inducers: Drugs like rifabutin decrease rilpivirine levels. If co-administered, rilpivirine dose should be increased to 50 mg daily, and reduced back to 25 mg daily when rifabutin is discontinued. 28. Stem Cell Mobilization Therapies: Antiretroviral medications, including rilpivirine, may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous stem cell products. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 29. QTc Monitoring: For drugs that increase QTc interval, such as macimorelin, ECG monitoring is recommended. Avoid co-administration if possible. 30. Adrenergic Agonists: Drugs like vilanterol may potentiate cardiovascular effects when co-administered with rilpivirine. Use caution. In summary, rilpivirine has significant interactions with drugs that affect gastric pH, CYP3A4 metabolism, and QTc interval. Careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of co-administration may be necessary to prevent treatment failure or toxicity.
